newsitem.title: USA: KeyCorp cuts 2,700 jobs in restructuring.
newsitem.headline: KeyCorp cuts 2,700 jobs in restructuring.

text.p: KeyCorp, moving to consolidate its operations from a 12-bank network into a single nationwide bank, said Monday it planned to take a $100 million charge and eliminate 2,700 jobs, or about 10 percent of its work force.

The company, which currently operates 12 banks in 14 states, also said that as part of the restructuring, it planned to sell more than 140 of its branch offices. Those to be sold, known as KeyCenters, are primarily in rural areas, and their sale will leave the bank with about 1,000 branch offices.

"We think the greater risk is on the revenue side," said analyst Sandra Flannigan of Merrill Lynch & Co. She said the company will have to keep revenue growth going while engaged in reducing its branch banking system.

The ratings agency Standard & Poor's noted that since the 1994 merger of Albany, N.Y.-based Key and Cleveland-based Society Corp., the company has experienced "lackluster revenue dynamics" despite its retail presence in the fairly strong Midwest and Rocky Mountain regions.
S&P said KeyCorp has been bolstering profitabilty through recognition of gains on sales of assets and other non-recurring items.

KeyCorp, which has about $65 billion in assets, said it will take the $100 million charge in the fourth quarter but expected to realise about $110 million in annual earnings benefits by the end of next year.
The Cleveland-based company also said its board authorised a new share buyback programme, effective immediately, in which up to 12 million shares may be repurchased by the end of 1997.

KeyCorp said the new bank will emphasise community and corporate banking products and services and will complement the delivery of consumer finance products through KeyBank USA, which will remain as a separate company.
"These are bold steps that will complete the process we launched 18 months ago to transform Key into a nationwide financial services provider," Chairman Robert Gillespie said in a statement.
"These actions will accelerate our schedule for completion of these tasks and position Key among the top-performing financial services companies in terms of both productivity and earnings growth."

KeyCorp said the work force reductions will be distributed throughout the company and its regions and be represented in all job levels. Affected employees will be eligible for other open positions within the company or be offered separation assistance, it said.

"We aim to be a national provider (of financial services)," said Bill Murschel, a KeyCorp spokesman. He said the company's KeyBank USA consumer finance unit already competes in most of the nation, doing business beyond the 14 states where it operates through 12 charters.
KeyBank USA is involved in such areas as credit cards, educational loans and auto lending, and Murschel said it wanted to have a national brand.

First Albany Co. analyst Kevin Timmons, noting Keycorp's plans to sell some branches and consolidate others, said, "the banking business is in the process of moving from physicial delivery of services at branches to electronic delivery."
KeyCorp's stock added $2.375 to end at $51.25 on the New York Stock Exchange.
